# bookstack

![Version: 5.7.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Version-5.7.0-informational?style=flat-square) ![Type: application](https://img.shields.io/badge/Type-application-informational?style=flat-square) ![AppVersion: version-v26.05.2](https://img.shields.io/badge/AppVersion-version--v26.05.2-informational?style=flat-square) ![Kubernetes: >=1.21.0-0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kubernetes-%3E%3D1.21.0--0-informational?style=flat-square)

bookstack documentation platform

## Requirements

| Repository | Name | Version |
|------------|------|---------|
| oci://registry-1.docker.io/cloudpirates | mariadb | 0.16.5 |
| oci://registry-1.docker.io/homeylabcharts | bookstack-file-exporter | 1.2.0 |

This chart is useful for demoing and light usage. Chart revisions may jump versions, it is recommended to use a dedicated mariadb instance instead and upgrade bookstack incrementally if using this chart for teams or production.

*Note: You should set some chart values by creating your own values.yaml and save that locally*

## Add Chart Repo
```bash
helm repo add homeylab https://homeylab.github.io/helm-charts/
# update the chart, this can also be run to pull new versions of the chart for upgrades
helm repo update homeylab
```

## Prerequisites
Ensure you either enable the mariadb dependency, `mariadb.enabled`, or have an existing compatible DB server ready for bookstack.

This chart provides the option to install mariadb by default from [CloudPirates](https://github.com/CloudPirates-io/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/mariadb).

## Install
```bash
helm install bookstack homeylab/bookstack -n bookstack --create-namespace

# with own values file - recommended
helm install -f my-values.yaml bookstack homeylab/bookstack -n bookstack --create-namespace
```

### OCI Registry Support
```bash
helm install bookstack -n bookstack oci://registry-1.docker.io/homeylabcharts/bookstack --version X.Y.Z --create-namespace

# with own values file - recommended
helm install -f my-values.yaml bookstack -n bookstack oci://registry-1.docker.io/homeylabcharts/bookstack --version X.Y.Z --create-namespace
```

### Install Example
Only some options are shown, view `values.yaml` for an exhaustive list.

<details closed>
<summary>custom-values.yaml</summary>
<br>

```yaml
# custom-values.yaml
image:
  # defaults to lscr.io/linuxserver/bookstack; override registry/repository/tag to pin a specific build
  tag: ""

linuxserver:
  enabled: true
  PUID: 1000
  PGID: 1000
  UMASK: "022"
  TZ: Etc/UTC

config:
  appUrl: "https://bookstack.somedomain"
  ## Leave appKey empty to auto-generate one (persisted in the chart Secret across upgrades).
  ## If you are upgrading a chart install that already has data, set this to your CURRENT key
  ## instead - see the 5.0.0 upgrade notes linked from the Breaking Changes table.
  appKey: ""
  ## Default values below will work with included mariadb chart in bookstack namespace
  dbHost: bookstack-mariadb.bookstack.svc.cluster.local
  dbPort: 3306
  dbDatabase: bookstack
  cacheDriver: database
  sessionDriver: database

extraEnv:
  APP_DEFAULT_DARK_MODE: true
  APP_VIEWS_BOOKS: list

ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: "nginx"
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-connect-timeout: "36000"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "36000"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "36000"
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: "letsencrypt-issuer"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/force-ssl-redirect: "true"
  hosts:
    - host: bookstack.somedomain
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix

## Alternative to ingress - Gateway API HTTPRoute (chart does NOT create the Gateway)
# httproute:
#   enabled: true
#   parentRefs:
#     - name: my-gateway
#       namespace: gateway-system
#   hostnames:
#     - bookstack.somedomain

persistence:
  enabled: true
  storageClass: ""
  size: 5Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce

## https://github.com/CloudPirates-io/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/mariadb
## some basic options below but look at their chart for more
mariadb:
  enabled: true
  auth:
    rootPassword: "root"
    existingSecret: ""
    database: "bookstack"
    username: "sampleuser"
    password: "samplepass"
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    storageClass: ""
    accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
    size: 5Gi
```

## Upgrade
It is recommended to make a backup of the mariadb database and also configuration files used by bookstack on its pvc. See [Backup and Restore](#backup-and-restore-of-mariadb) section for more details.

For additional steps that need to be done for upgrade, check upstream dependencies:
1. For Bookstack upgrade steps, check the [documentation](https://www.bookstackapp.com/docs/admin/updates/).
2. If using the mariadb instance provided in this chart, follow the CloudPirates mariadb chart [upgrade](https://github.com/CloudPirates-io/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/mariadb) steps for DB upgrades and follow official Mariadb [guides](https://mariadb.com/kb/en/upgrading/).

```bash
helm upgrade bookstack homeylab/bookstack -n bookstack

# with own values file - recommended
helm upgrade -f my-values.yaml bookstack homeylab/bookstack -n bookstack
```

### OCI Registry Support
```bash
helm upgrade bookstack -n bookstack oci://registry-1.docker.io/homeylabcharts/bookstack --version X.Y.Z

# with own values file - recommended
helm upgrade -f my-values.yaml bookstack -n bookstack oci://registry-1.docker.io/homeylabcharts/bookstack --version X.Y.Z
```

### Nginx Configuration Warnings
After certain upgrades, you may see warnings in the logs about nginx configuration mismatches.
```
**** The following active confs have different version dates than the samples that are shipped. ****
**** This may be due to user customization or an update to the samples. ****
**** You should compare the following files to the samples in the same folder and update them. ****
**** Use the link at the top of the file to view the changelog. ****
┌────────────┬────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  old date  │  new date  │ path                                                                   │
├────────────┼────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 2024-05-27 │ 2024-07-16 │ /config/nginx/site-confs/default.conf                                  │
└────────────┴────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Linuxserver.io changes their base Nginx configuration at times and it may have drifted. You can either find the new versions being referenced [here](https://github.com/linuxserver/docker-baseimage-alpine-nginx) or if your environment has access, it can be pulled. You can then copy the new version using `kubectl cp` to the pod and replace the old version. To re-pull it on start up, you can delete the file. Either option will require a restart of the pod to take effect.

```bash
# example of deleting for a re-pull
kubectl exec -it -n bookstack {{ pod_name }} -- bash -c "rm /config/nginx/site-confs/default.conf"

# example of copying a new version
kubectl cp default.conf bookstack/{{ pod_name }}:/config/nginx/site-confs/default.conf
```

### Breaking Changes

| Start Chart Version | Target Chart Version | Upgrade Steps |
| ------------------- | -------------------- | ------------- |
| `4.1.X` | `5.0.0` | Major breaking revision — embedded mariadb dependency swapped (Bitnami → CloudPirates), credentials/APP_KEY moved to a chart-managed Secret, and BookStack updated to `version-v26.05.2`. **Read the [upgrade notes](https://github.com/homeylab/helm-charts/blob/main/charts/bookstack/docs/upgrade.md#from-41x-to-500) in full before upgrading** if you have existing data. |

_The [full upgrade notes](https://github.com/homeylab/helm-charts/blob/main/charts/bookstack/docs/upgrade.md) cover every version, including upgrades gated on opt-in settings._

For more configuration options, refer to the documented env variables available for bookstack [here](https://github.com/BookStackApp/BookStack/blob/development/.env.example.complete).

Additional configuration can be specified in the `extraEnv` section, some examples:
```yaml
extraEnv:
  TZ: Etc/UTC
  APP_DEFAULT_DARK_MODE: true
  APP_VIEWS_BOOKS: list
```

## Bookstack File Exporter (Backup Your Pages)
This chart includes an optional [exporter](https://github.com/homeylab/bookstack-file-exporter) that will archive all your pages and their contents to a supported object storage provider(s) like minio, s3, etc.

This exporter creates a `.tgz` archive in a folder-tree layout to maintain the hierarchy of shelves, books, and pages. Including the option to export media such as images and attachments.

The exporter is included as an optional dependency from a different helm [chart](https://github.com/homeylab/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/bookstack-file-exporter) and is enabled by setting `bookstack-file-exporter.enabled`. Only a minimal set of `bookstack-file-exporter.*` values are surfaced above (the URL and credentials most users need); the subchart's own `config:` block is snake_case and matches its upstream `config.yml` 1:1 - see the [bookstack-file-exporter chart's values.yaml/README](https://github.com/homeylab/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/bookstack-file-exporter) for the full schema and defaults.

## Backup And Restore Of MariaDB
Back up the database **and bookstack's own files** before upgrading, and before operations like resizing a PVC or changing `storageClass`. The database dump does not cover the `/config` PVC — uploaded images, page attachments and custom themes live there. Follow the upstream procedures for the actual backup and restore steps: [BookStack](https://www.bookstackapp.com/docs/admin/backup-restore/) and [MariaDB](https://mariadb.com/kb/en/full-backup-and-restore-with-mariabackup/).

The details specific to this chart:

- Scale BookStack down first so nothing writes during the dump: `kubectl scale deploy -n bookstack bookstack --replicas=0`
- The embedded database pod is `bookstack-mariadb-0` and the database is named `bookstack`
- The `root` password is generated into a chart-managed `Secret` at install unless you set it yourself
- Keep BookStack at zero replicas for the whole window — dump, upgrade, restore — then scale it back up. If an upgrade restarts the pod part-way through, scale it down again before continuing

> **Note** - a logical dump copied out with `kubectl cp` only suits a small install: it writes to the pod's ephemeral storage and holds BookStack down for the whole window. For anything larger prefer a volume-level backup — [Longhorn](https://longhorn.io/docs/latest/) or your CSI driver's snapshots.
